findings.description: The RDS instance explicitly sets `storage_encrypted = false`, leaving database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and replicas derived from it unencrypted at rest.

The RDS instance sets `publicly_accessible = true`, assigning a public endpoint/IP-capable network interface and unnecessarily exposing the database to internet-reachable network paths. The attached rule currently limits port 3306 to the VPC CIDR, but public accessibility weakens the intended network boundary.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports to `0.0.0.0/0`. This violates least-privilege network egress and permits unrestricted outbound connections from the database network interface if it is compromised.

The EC2 instance role is granted `s3:*`, `ec2:*`, and `rds:*` against every resource. Any compromise of the attached instance can obtain credentials capable of broad data access and infrastructure modification, including potentially destructive or privilege-escalating actions.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written as plaintext PHP configuration at `/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc`. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and may be retained in Terraform state, while the deployed file exposes the credential to processes/users able to read it.

The application connects to MySQL with `mysqli_connect` without SSL/TLS parameters, and the RDS parameter group does not enforce secure transport. Database credentials and application data can therefore traverse the VPC network without verified encryption in transit.
